The In-Bi eutectic near 345 K does not freeze into pure elements but into In2Bi intermetallic plus an In-rich solid solution, so the computed difference includes the nonzero In2Bi formation enthalpy and liquid mixing enthalpy rather than the eutectic melting enthalpy. This is a systematic phase-reference error that biases the latent heat, not a sampling or threshold quibble, so the rules referee's checklist pass does not address it. The timestep, cell size, ensemble and temperature are otherwise acceptable.. Fix: Construct the actual eutectic solid reference (In2Bi crystal plus In-rich solid solution in lever-rule proportions), equilibrate it in NPT at 345 K, and take the enthalpy difference against the liquid at the same composition and temperature; alternatively use a two-phase coexistence approach. Run multiple seeds to obtain a meaningful uncertainty. [claude-fable-5-1, $0.0468])

The real solid of Field's metal (Bi32.5In51Sn16.5) is a eutectic of intermetallic phases (BiIn2 and an In–Sn γ/β solid solution), not elemental Bi, In and Sn. This reference choice, which the agent's own flag records, folds the formation enthalpies of those intermetallics and the liquid mixing enthalpy into the reported value. That biases the latent heat by an amount comparable to the reported uncertainty or larger. [llm audit] The latent heat is the enthalpy of the liquid alloy minus the enthalpy of pure In and pure Bi solids, as the agent's own flag 'eutectic_solid_assumed_pure_elements' admits. The In-33.7 wt% Bi eutectic at about 345 K solidifies into the intermetallic In2Bi plus an In-rich solid solution, not into the pure elements. In2Bi has a nonzero (negative) formation enthalpy, and the liquid has its own mixing enthalpy. The computed number therefore includes these formation and mixing terms rather than the melting enthalpy of the eutectic solid, a mismatched-phase latent heat that biases the value. The model choice, the 2 fs timestep for heavy In/Bi atoms, the 500-atom cell and the evaluation temperature are otherwise reasonable.. Fix: Build the actual eutectic solid as the reference: an In2Bi crystal plus an In-rich solid solution, in proportions set by the lever rule. Run NPT on that solid at 345 K, alongside the liquid at the same composition and temperature, and take the enthalpy difference. Alternatively, run two-phase coexistence of the eutectic solid and the liquid. Use multiple seeds for the uncertainty. [claude-opus-5-5, $0.0219]
